limitations: All queries use preexisting frozen graphs. Equal responses prove preservation on these questions, not source-truth or improved graph quality.
The query controls compare two Compass binaries. They do not execute Graphify or show broad superiority.
The missing Redux path identity remains unavailable, with no substitute endpoint.
Thirty-one warm queries regress by more than ten percent: all six lightweight questions on each of five language graphs and CloudStack graph_stats. All per-query cold and warm durations are retained.
Large-graph memory is incomplete because the timing wrapper was terminated during five CloudStack session teardowns. No paired CloudStack peak-memory conclusion is supported.
Five-language mixed-query sessions show higher candidate peak RSS. This is a real local cost for the tested workload.
The default-low core integration failures reproduce on the unchanged committed baseline; their proposed inference-level explanation is unverified in this review.
Known development repositories and changed-cache fixtures do not provide an independent final quality holdout.
scope: Standalone JSON graph freshness and fixed source-query preservation/cost controls, not a Graphify superiority score.
